subject: F3 ail input produces choppy haplotype reconstructions

messages.author: 90b86c41c3f69251
messages.subject: F3 ail input produces choppy haplotype reconstructions
parts:
I usually process DO and CC crosses and have no trouble with them. But I’m working with a C57BL/6J x DBA/2J F3 and I’m having trouble getting good haplotype reconstructions.  I’ve read the docs and complied with them to the best of my knowledge. I’m using an “ail” cross type with “ngen” = 3. All mice are the same direction of cross. I’ve checked the order of the marker maps and the genotypes, formatting, etc. When I read in the cross, reconstruct the genomes, and phase them, I get a plot with way too many fine crossovers.

 

cross = read_cross2(file = file.path(out_dir, 'bxd_f3.json'), quiet = FALSE)

probs = calc_genoprob(cross = cross, map = cross$gmap, cores = 4)

gt    = maxmarg(probs = probs, minprob = 0.1)

gt_ph = guess_phase(cross = cross, geno = gt)

plot_onegeno(geno = gt_ph, map = cross$pmap)

 

This is my JSON control file.

 

{

    "description": "BXD F3 chr 1 only",

    "crosstype": "ail",

    "sep": ",",

    "na.strings": ["-", "NA"],

    "comment.char": "#",

    "geno": "geno.csv",

    "founder_geno": "foundergeno.csv",

    "gmap": "gmap.csv",

    "pmap": "pmap.csv",

    "pheno": "pheno.csv",

    "covar": "covar.csv",

    "genotypes": {

      "A": 1,

      "H": 2,

      "B": 3

    },

    "alleles": ["A", "B"],

    "geno_transposed": true,

    "founder_geno_transposed": true,

    "sex": {

      "covar": "Sex",

      "female": "female",

      "male": "male"

    },

    "cross_info": {

      "file": "crossinfo.csv"

    }

  }

 

Frustratingly, when I use the ‘genail2’ model, the reconstructions look just fine. But I want to use the correct model for the cross.

 

I’m attaching a zip file with my qtl2 input files for two samples and one chromosome.  (Which may get stripped out by Google…)

 

Any thoughts about what else to check in my input?

 

Dan

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] F3 ail input produces choppy haplotype reconstructions
parts:
Hi, Dan,

For two-way crosses like AIL, the founder genotypes are not used, but instead you need to re-code the genotypes so that 1 = homozygous parent 1 and 3 = homozygous parent 2.

genail2, on the other hand, does use those founder genotypes, and so the genotypes don't need to be re-coded.

karl
